EDING.label: -ed / -ing 감정 형용사
EDING.tip: 내가 느끼면 -ed (I felt bored / I was inspired), 사물·상황이 느끼게 하면 -ing (It was boring / inspiring / challenging).

COMP.label: 비교급
COMP.tip: 긴 형용사는 more ~ than, 짧은 형용사는 -er (simpler, easier). '아주 더'는 very가 아니라 much more.

TENSE.label: 과거 이야기 시제
TENSE.tip: 경험(STAR) 답변은 처음부터 끝까지 과거형: felt, didn't need, was.

POS.label: 품사
POS.tip: 동사를 꾸미면 부사(quickly, flexibly), be·feel 뒤는 형용사(anxious, advantageous), 명사 앞엔 관사(an advantage).

PREP.label: 전치사
PREP.tip: 동사·형용사와 짝인 전치사를 통째로 외운다: sign up for, related to, helpful for, at a university, at night, downtown(전치사 없음).

ART.label: 관사·복수
ART.tip: 셀 수 있는 단수 명사엔 a/the, 일반적인 것은 복수: at a cafe, a kindergarten, all universities.

OBJ.label: 목적어 빠짐
OBJ.tip: inform / ask / remind 뒤엔 사람: inform you about, ask you to, remind me to.

SVA.label: 주어-동사 수일치
SVA.tip: every·each + 단수 동사 (every student has), 복수 주어 + 복수 동사 (online classes are).

KOR.label: 한국어식 표현
KOR.tip: '~해야 했다'는 had to, '보통 ~한다'는 typically. should는 조언·의무에만.

LINK.label: 연결어
LINK.tip: Although/While 문장엔 but을 같이 쓰지 않는다. Therefore는 진짜 결과일 때만, Nevertheless는 대조일 때만.

COLL.label: 단어 조합
COLL.tip: 자연스러운 짝으로: improve the quality of our lives, lead to + 명사/-ing, affect people(전치사 없음).

SPELL.label: 철자
SPELL.tip: 시험엔 맞춤법 검사가 없다. 마지막 1분은 철자만 본다.

email.subject: Great place to fix your bike brakes
email.scenario: You recently visited the newly opened campus bicycle repair co-op to fix a flat tire. You found the student volunteers very helpful and noticed that all the repair tools are free for students to use. Your friend Sam commutes to classes by bike and recently complained about having squeaky brakes.
tasks: Describe your experience at the campus bicycle repair co-op.
Explain why Sam should take their bike to the co-op.
Suggest a specific day to go there together.
email.mine:
Dear Sam,

I hope this email finds you well.

Recently, I visited the newly opened campus bicycle repair co-op to fix a flat tire. In the shop, the staff members were so kind and worked professionally. After the service, I thought about you commuting to classes by bike and complaining about having squeaky brakes recently. In addition, the tools and using the shop are totally free, so I think you should take your bike there to deal with the problem. Therefore, how about visiting the bicycle repair co-op together on Saturday? If possible, please let me know what is the best time for you. I am looking forward to your reply.

Best regards,
Taebin Yoo

Dear Ms. Thompson,

I hope this email finds you well.
I am writing to inform the plan of the campaign.

This morning, I have just created the initial plan for the campaign. The main idea is advertising your new cloth on Seoul Station. I think this is an effective opportunity to advertise to many people. This is because almost 100,000 people visit to Seoul Station everyday. If possible, please let me know your opinion and any suggestions for improvement. I would appreciate it if you could replay at your earliest conveninece.

Best regards,
Marketing Team
Taebin Yoo

Best regards,
Taebin Yoo
Marketing Team

email.subject: A place to visit in Seoul
email.scenario: Your friend Sarah is visiting Seoul for the first time next month. She asked you to recommend a place she should see.
tasks: Recommend one place and explain how to get there.
Explain why the place is worth visiting.
Suggest meeting up while she is in Seoul.
email.mine:
Dear Sarah,

I hope this email finds you well. I am writing to suggest the place where you want to go sightseeing in Seoul. Recently, I heard that you are visiting Seoul for the first time. Thus, I want to recommend the Namsan Tower in Seoul. It is located in downtown. You can take a bus or subway to Namsan tower. If you arrive here, you can see the great city view in Seoul. I recommend that you visit at the night. In addition, I hope we can hang out toghther. Please let me know what time is the best for you. Have a nice trip in Seoul!

Best regards,

Taebin Yoo
email.tutor:
Dear Sarah,

I hope this email finds you well.

Recently, I heard that you are visiting Seoul for the first time. I am writing to suggest a place where you should go sightseeing in Seoul. I want to recommend Namsan Tower in Seoul. It is located downtown, and you can take a bus or subway to get there. Once you arrive, you can see the great city view of Seoul, and you can eat traditional food nearby, as there are a lot of restaurants in the area. I recommend that you visit at night. In addition, I hope we can hang out together. Please let me know what is the best time for you. Have a nice trip in Seoul!
Best regards,

Taebin Yoo

prof.name: Dr. Alvarez
prof.text: This week, we are evaluating school calendar designs. Many educational systems follow a traditional calendar featuring a long summer vacation of two or three months. However, some districts have shifted to a year-round calendar. In a year-round system, students attend school for the same total number of days, but their time off is distributed into multiple shorter breaks throughout the year—such as a three-week break every season. I would like you to discuss which approach you think is better for students. Does the traditional long summer break provide essential benefits, or is a year-round schedule with frequent, shorter breaks more advantageous?

students.name: Liam
students.text: I strongly prefer the traditional calendar with a long summer break. Students undergo a tremendous amount of stress during the academic year, and they need a significant, uninterrupted block of time to truly decompress. Furthermore, a long summer allows teenagers to get part-time jobs, attend specialized summer camps, or travel extensively with their families. These real-world experiences are just as important for a student's overall development as classroom learning.

students.name: Maya
students.text: I have to disagree with Liam. The biggest issue with a long summer break is what educators call the 'summer slide.' Students often forget a large portion of the material they learned the previous year, forcing teachers to spend the first month of the new term reviewing old topics. A year-round schedule prevents this knowledge loss. Plus, having frequent, shorter breaks throughout the year prevents burnout much more effectively than waiting nine exhausting months for a vacation.

prof.name: Professor Thorne
prof.text: Welcome to our Business Management seminar. Today, we are discussing emerging trends in corporate structuring. Recently, several high-profile companies have tested a four-day workweek. In this model, employees work thirty-two hours over four days but receive the same compensation as a traditional forty-hour, five-day week. Proponents argue this arrangement improves work-life balance, while critics worry about a drop in overall productivity and operational coverage. Do you think adopting a four-day workweek is a smart long-term strategy for businesses? Why or why not?

students.name: Elena
students.text: I strongly believe that a four-day workweek is a great strategy. Employee burnout is a massive problem right now, leading to frequent mistakes and low morale. If people have a three-day weekend to truly disconnect and spend time with their families, they will return to work highly motivated. Because they are well-rested and energized, they can actually complete the same amount of work in four days as they previously did in five.

students.name: David
students.text: I disagree. While a four-day workweek sounds nice in theory, it just isn't practical for most businesses. Think about logistics companies, customer support centers, or retail stores—they need to be available to clients every single day. If a company reduces everyone's hours, management will be forced to hire additional staff just to cover the missing shifts. This would significantly increase payroll costs and ultimately make the business less competitive.

discussion.note: 튜터: 같은 비용으로 여러 콘텐츠를 누릴 수 있다는 점에 집중한 전략 — Good!

prof.name: Professor Gupta
prof.text: Welcome, everyone. This week, we are looking at pricing strategies, specifically the widespread shift toward subscription-based models. In the past, consumers usually paid a one-time fee to own a product outright, such as a software program, a video game, or an album. Today, many companies instead charge a recurring monthly or annual fee for ongoing access to their products or services. I'd like to hear your thoughts on this trend. Do you think the shift toward subscription models is ultimately beneficial for consumers, or does it do more harm than good?

students.name: Alex
students.text: I believe subscription models are great for consumers because they significantly lower the initial cost of access. Instead of paying hundreds of dollars upfront for professional software or a massive media library, anyone can afford a small monthly fee. Plus, companies are incentivized to constantly improve their services and provide regular updates to keep their subscribers happy, so we always get the most updated version of the product.

students.name: Maria
students.text: I have to disagree. I think the subscription model is harmful because it usually costs consumers much more in the long run. There is also the issue of ownership; you never actually own the product. If you face financial trouble and have to cancel your subscription, you lose access to everything immediately. A one-time purchase gives consumers permanent ownership and much more control over their personal budgets.

prof.name: Dr. Kim
prof.text: Many people today care a great deal about how they look, and spending on beauty products keeps rising. What do you think is the main reason people care so much about their appearance? Is it social media, advertising, or something else?

students.name: Jan
students.text: I think social media plays the biggest role. People are constantly bombarded with images of perfect bodies and faces, and they start comparing themselves with these images every day.

students.name: Kyle
students.text: I would point to advertising. Beauty companies spend billions on ads that tell us we are not good enough unless we buy their products. Social media is just one more place to show those ads.

discussion.mine: Both Jan and Kyle made valid points, but I lean toward Jan's view. I agree with the notion that social media plays the biggest role. This is because people are constantly bombarded with impages of perfect bodies and faces. I would add that perfect appearance image is important when we make a relationship on social media. For example, when I watch on instagrams, I usually follow some influencers who have a pretty appearance. If they upload on pretty appearance pictures, it can ultimately lead to following their accounts. In addition, I believe it can lead to put pressure on them about good images. For theses reasons, I believe social media affects to people caring so much about their appearance.
discussion.tutor: Both Jan and Kyle made valid points, but I lean toward Jan's view. I agree with the notion that social media plays the biggest role. This is because people are constantly bombarded with images of perfect bodies and faces. I would add that perfect appearance is important when we choose to form relationships on social media. For example, when I look at Instagram, I usually choose to follow influencers who have a pretty appearance. If they upload pretty pictures, it can ultimately lead to me following their accounts. In addition, I believe that this dynamic can put pressure on them to maintain a good image. For these reasons, I believe social media affects people and causes them to care so much about their appearance.

prof.name: Professor Lewis
prof.text: In our sociology class this week, we are discussing the difficulties that young adults face. In your opinion, what is the biggest problem that young people face in contemporary society? Why?

students.name: Sienna
students.text: I think the biggest problem is the cost of housing. Rent in big cities has become so expensive that many young people cannot afford to live on their own, even with a full-time job.

students.name: Ryan
students.text: For me, it is mental health. Young people feel constant pressure to succeed, and social media makes them compare themselves with others all the time.

discussion.mine: While both Sienna and Ryan made valid points, but I believe the lack of hiring is the biggest problem in contemporary society. Many younger generation encounters do not have enough opportunities in field. First, as we live in a technologically advanced world, companies do not want to hire beginner members. This is because artificial intelligence tools can replace beginner member's work. Furthermore, these tools help companies save time and money. Therefore, I believe governments should encourage internship programs to get a job for young generations. Through internship programs, companies can get high qualified people easily and young generation can get more experiences that AI tools do not have.
discussion.tutor: While both Siena and Ryan made valid points, I believe the lack of hiring is the biggest problem in contemporary society. Many members of the younger generation do not have enough opportunities in the field. First, as we live in a technologically advanced world, companies do not want to hire inexperienced people. This is because artificial intelligence tools can replace new graduates' work. Furthermore, these tools help companies save time and money. Therefore, I believe governments should encourage internship programs to help members of the younger generation land a job. Through such programs, companies can get highly qualified people easily and the younger generation can get more experience that AI tools do not have.

discussion.note: 튜터가 주제 문장을 'COVID-19'에서 'the rise of online communication'(문화적 변화)으로 바꿨다 — 질문의 핵심 명사에 맞춰 답하기.

prof.name: Dr. Patel
prof.text: Over the last 200 years, societies around the world have changed dramatically. In your opinion, what is the most important cultural change that has happened during this period? Explain why.

students.name: Jeremy
students.text: I would say the spread of electricity. It changed when people work and sleep, how they spend their evenings, and it made almost every modern technology possible.

students.name: Saki
students.text: I think the most important change is that women gained access to education and the right to vote. This completely changed families, workplaces, and politics.

discussion.mine: Both Jeremy and Saki made valid points, but I think COVID-19 is the most important one that changes our society from the last 200 years. This is because COVID-19 made humans' daily lives more friendly. For example, in COVID-19, governments regulated meetings in person in order to prevent spreading illness. Therefore, many industries started to use online meeting platforms, such as Google meeting and Zoom. It helps people use online meeting platforms more frequently. In addition, many companies started to focus on developing technology tools. For these reasons, I believe COVID-19 affects our lives in technologically advanced world.
discussion.tutor: Both Jeremy and Saki made valid points, but I think the rise of online communication is one of the biggest cultural changes our society has undergone in the last 200 years. The change was in large part brought about or encouraged by COVID-19, and this is because COVID-19 made humans' daily lives more tech-friendly. For example, during COVID-19, governments regulated in-person meetings in order to prevent spreading illness. Therefore, many industries started to use online meeting platforms, such as Google Meet and Zoom. They help people use online meeting platforms more frequently. In addition, many companies started to focus on developing technology tools. For these reasons, I believe the rise of online communication has affected our lives and moved us into a more technologically advanced world.

prof.name: Dr. Nguyen
prof.text: Scientists can now genetically modify mosquitoes so that the populations that spread malaria and dengue fever die out. Some people see this as a powerful way to save lives, while others worry about the effects on ecosystems. Should we use genetic engineering to eliminate these mosquito populations? Why or why not?

students.name: Maya
students.text: Yes. Millions of people get sick from these diseases every year. If we have the technology to stop them, we should use it. People are more important than insects!

students.name: David
students.text: I am not so sure. Mosquitoes are food for birds, fish, and bats. If we remove them, we could damage entire ecosystems in ways we cannot predict.

discussion.mine: Both Maya and David made valid points, but I lean toward Maya's view. I agree with the notion that we should use genetic engineering to improve our quality of lives. This is because genetic engineering is directly related with saving people from serious diseases. For example, nowadays, many diseases cannot be eliminated by only using general medicine. However, if scientists use genetic engineering, they can eliminate it easily. Furthermore, it is important for old generations. According to recent research, old generations have a lower percent of survival when they got malaria and dengue fever. For these reasons, I believe that we should eradicate specific populations of mosquitoes to stop the spread of deadly diseases by using genetic engineering.
discussion.tutor: Both Maya and David made valid points, but I lean toward Maya's view. I agree with the notion that we should use genetic engineering to improve the quality of our lives. This is because genetic engineering is directly related to saving people from serious diseases. For example, nowadays, many diseases cannot be eliminated only by the use of common, readily available medicines. However, if scientists use genetic engineering, they can eliminate such diseases easily. Furthermore, it is doubly important for older generations, because according to recent research, older people have a lower survival rate when they catch malaria and dengue fever, for example. For these reasons, I believe that we should eradicate specific populations of mosquitoes to stop the spread of deadly diseases by using genetic engineering. To paraphrase Maya, people are more important than insects!

prof.name: Professor Ortiz
prof.text: Cities keep growing, and governments must decide how to use land. Some argue that urban development is necessary for a better quality of life, while others believe protecting natural areas should come first. Which should governments prioritize, and why?

students.name: Andrew
students.text: Governments should protect natural areas first. Once a forest or wetland is destroyed, it is gone forever, and we lose clean air, water, and wildlife.

students.name: Claire
students.text: I think development should come first. People need housing, transportation, and jobs. Without new infrastructure, cities become crowded and expensive.

discussion.mine: Both Andrew and Claire made valid points, but I lean toward Claire's view. I agree with the notion that urbanization is necessary for improving quality of life. This is because it is directly related to citizens' economy. As Andrew mentioned, if we focus too much on preservation, citizens should pay more taxes and consider a lot of regulations in their daily lives. For example, in Korea, the government regulated to develop some cities' infrastructures for preserving ecosystems. Therefore, citizens had to pay more taxes for this preservation system and felt uncomfortable by less infrastructures. I think it can be a serious economic burden, especially for poor family. For these reasons, I believe the government should focus on developing urbanization for citizens.
discussion.tutor: Both Andrew and Claire made valid points, but I lean toward Claire's view. I agree with the notion that urbanization is necessary for improving quality of life. This is because it is directly related to citizens' economic interests. If we focus too much on preservation, citizens should pay more taxes and consider a lot of regulations in their daily lives. For example, in Korea, the government regulated the development of some cities' infrastructures in order to preserve ecosystems. Therefore, citizens had to pay more taxes for this preservation and felt uncomfortable because of less developed infrastructure. I think it can be a serious economic burden, especially for poor families. For these reasons, I believe the government should focus on developing urbanization for citizens.

prof.name: Dr. Reed
prof.text: More and more people pay with cards and phones instead of cash, and some countries are moving toward a completely cashless society. Do you think a cashless society is beneficial? Why or why not?

students.name: Elena
students.text: A cashless society is absolutely beneficial. Payments are faster and safer, and we no longer need to carry wallets full of coins.

students.name: Malik
students.text: I worry about people who are left behind. Many elderly people are not comfortable with apps, and digital payments let companies track everything we buy.

discussion.mine: Both Elena and Malik made valid points, but I lean toward Elena's view. I agree with the notion that a cashless society is absolutely beneficial in our daily lives. This is because it can save our time and money. In the past, we should check out bills from banks. However, nowadays, many people use mobile transfer services and credit cards for economic activities. For example, in Korea, when people take public transportation, they should pay only for credit cards and mobile payment. It can reduce heavy traffic because people do not need to pay and count paper cash. Furthermore, it made people reduce visiting banks and feel convenience. If governments encourage people to become a cashless society, many people can save time to find and calculate paper cash. For these reasons, I believe a cashless society will be advantageous for everyone.
discussion.tutor: Both Elena and Malik made valid points, but I lean toward Elena's view. I agree with the notion that a cashless society is absolutely beneficial in our daily lives. This is because it can save our time and money. In the past, we had to withdraw cash from banks. However, nowadays, many people use mobile transfer services and credit cards for economic activities. For example, in Korea, when people take public transportation, they typically pay only by credit cards and mobile payments. This practice can reduce heavy traffic because people do not need to pay and count paper cash. Furthermore, it has made people reduce visits to banks and increased their convenience. If governments encourage people to accept a cashless society, they can save time finding and calculating paper cash. For these reasons, I believe a cashless society will be advantageous for everyone.

prof.name: Professor Hayes
prof.text: To deal with climate change, some people argue that we should focus on sustainable solutions here on Earth, while others believe we should invest in technologies such as space colonization as a backup plan for humanity. Which approach should we prioritize? Why?

students.name: Paul
students.text: We should invest in space colonization. Earth's resources are limited, and having a second home for humanity is the only long-term guarantee of survival.

students.name: Kelly
students.text: Sustainable solutions should come first. Using less energy, choosing public transportation, and protecting forests are things we can do right now.

discussion.mine: Both Paul and Kelly made valid points, but I lean toward Kelly's view. I agree with the notion that we should prioritize sustainable solutions for climate change. This is because it is the most realistic solution for our future life. For example, if we reduce using private cars, we can keep our environments easily. Furthermore, these small activities are very easy to do immediately. Nevertheless, if governments invest in space colonization, it is risky and uncertain even though it requires a lot of taxes. For these reasons, I believe we should focus on small activities for our environments.
discussion.tutor: Both Paul and Kelly made valid points, but I lean toward Kelly's view. I agree with the notion that we should prioritize sustainable solutions for climate change. This is because it is the most realistic solution for our future life. For example, if we reduce the use of private cars, we can protect our environment effectively. Furthermore, these small activities are very practical to implement immediately compared to the huge challenge of colonizing another planet. In addition, if governments invest in space colonization, it is risky and uncertain because it requires a lot of taxes and therefore might not gain citizens' support. For these reasons, I believe we should focus on small activities to preserve our environment as soon as possible.

prof.name: Dr. Collins
prof.text: Many schools are now discussing how to integrate technology, especially AI tools, into education. Do you think using AI tools in the classroom will help students learn more effectively? Why or why not?

students.name: Hannah
students.text: I think AI tools are useful, but students might rely on them too much and stop thinking for themselves.

students.name: Marcus
students.text: Technology is already part of every job, so schools should teach students how to use AI tools well rather than avoid them.

discussion.mine: I believe utilizing AI tools to integrate technology into education is essential for students' productive learning. This is because AI tools can provide an effective guidance to improve their abilities. For example, when students set their study goal, they usually feel frustrated because every student have different backgrounds and each goal about their learning. However, AI tools can help them set individual study goal efficiently. Furthermore, AI tools can be used 24/7. Although students have questions while they study at night, they can ask and get a good answer by AI tools. For these reasons, I believe integrating technology into education will benefit for many students.
discussion.tutor: I believe utilizing AI tools to integrate technology into education is essential for students' productive learning because such tools can provide effective guidance to improve their abilities. For example, when students set their study goals, they usually feel frustrated because every student has a different background and individualized goals in their learning. However, AI tools can help them set individual study goals efficiently. Furthermore, the tools can be used 24/7. Even when students have questions while studying at night, they can ask and get a good answer from an AI tool. For these reasons, I believe integrating technology into education will benefit many students.

discussion.note: 튜터가 구체적인 예시(Batman의 Penguin)를 추가했다 — 이름이 있는 예시.

prof.name: Professor Wright
prof.text: In our literature course, we have been analyzing what makes stories memorable. When writers want to deliver a message, which is more effective in creating a compelling story: strong character development or an exciting plot? Explain your view.

students.name: Olivia
students.text: Plot matters most. If nothing interesting happens, readers stop reading before they ever get to know the characters.

students.name: Ben
students.text: I think characters are the heart of a story. We remember people like Harry Potter long after we forget the details of what happened.

discussion.mine: Many writers use their stories in order to express their message. I believe character development is the more effective way to deliever their message than plot in creating a compelling story. This is because it can include a lot of narrative factors what authors want. For example, if authors make strange billions in their novel, it can become an effective way to express directly many problems in our society. Furthermore, these story characteristics can help readers understand the author's messages more easily. For these reasons, I believe character development is the most important factor in storytelling.
discussion.tutor: Many writers use their stories in order to express their message. I believe character development is the more effective way to deliver these messages than plot in creating a compelling story. This is because it can include a lot of narrative factors that the authors want to express. For example, if an author creates a strange villain in their novel, it can become an effective way to indirectly express their opinions about many problems in our society. For example, the famous villain "the Penguin" from Batman represents the problem of excessive greed and its effects on society. Furthermore, these characteristics of the characters can help readers understand the author's messages more easily. For these reasons, I believe character development is the most important factor in storytelling.

discussion.note: 튜터가 '그래서 어떻게 되는가' 문장과 질문형 문장(where will the company's future leaders come from?)을 추가했다.

prof.name: Dr. Morgan
prof.text: In management, leaders use very different styles. Democratic leaders involve employees in decisions, while authoritarian leaders make decisions on their own and expect employees to follow them. Which leadership style do you think is more effective in the workplace? Why?

students.name: Andrew
students.text: Authoritarian leadership is more effective, especially in a crisis. Decisions are made quickly, and everyone knows exactly what to do.

students.name: Claire
students.text: Democratic leadership works better in the long run. When employees take part in decisions, they feel responsible for the results and work harder.

discussion.mine: Both Andrew and Claire made valid points, but I lean toward Claire's view. I strongly agree with the notion that democratic leadership is more effective than authoritarian leadership. This is because democratic leadership can give opportunities to develop themselves. For example, if many employees can participate in their work-decisions more directly, it can become helpful experiences to improve their results. According to recent research, many junior employees do not have enough opportunities to develop their skills since many bosses require to follow only their rules. Therefore, if companies implement the democratic leadership, I believe it will be a fascinating chance to develop employees' abilities.
discussion.tutor: Both Andrew and Claire made valid points, but I lean toward Claire's view. I strongly agree with the notion that democratic leadership is more effective than authoritarian leadership. This is because democratic leadership can give opportunities for employees to develop themselves. For example, if many employees can participate in their work-decisions more directly, it can improve their results in the workplace. When employees feel free to speak their opinions and work as a team, they are more productive and enjoy improved mental health as well. According to recent research, many junior employees do not have enough opportunities to develop their decision-making skills since many bosses require them to follow only the supervisor's rules. If employees never have a chance to develop such skills and participate in teamwork, where will the company's future leaders come from? Therefore, if companies implement democratic leadership, I believe it will be a fascinating chance to develop employees' abilities.

prof.name: Professor Allen
prof.text: Psychologists have studied for decades what makes people happy. Which factor do you think contributes most to a person's overall happiness: their career, their personal relationships, or their health? Why?

students.name: Sofia
students.text: Personal relationships matter most. Studies show that people with close friends and family live longer and feel happier, no matter how much money they make.

students.name: James
students.text: Health is the foundation of everything. If you are sick, it is hard to enjoy your job or your relationships.

discussion.mine: I believe that career is the most factor that contribute to human happiness because it can be lead to a lot of opportunities in our daily lives. For example, people can get a lot of money and develop their dreams through developing their career. Furthermore, when people get a job, they can also get the quality of personal relationships because they usually spend a lot of time with their coworkers. It can lead to networking events. According to recent research, many older generations feel blue after retirement. Therefore, I believe developing one's career is the largest impact on their overall happiness.
discussion.tutor: I believe that career is the most important factor that contributes to human happiness because it can lead to a lot of opportunities in our daily lives. For example, people can earn a lot of money and realize their dreams through improving their career. Furthermore, when people get a job, they can also enhance the quality of personal relationships because they usually spend a lot of time with their coworkers. A good company job can also lead to networking events, another opportunity to meet interesting people. According to recent research, many older generations feel blue after retirement; therefore, I believe developing one's career has the largest impact on a person's overall happiness.
